summary: A toggle for an on/off setting with its label, description and error laid out beside it, taking part in forms.

label.note: Visible label next to the track and accessible name. Required: shadow DOM keeps an external <label for> from naming the inner input.

hideLabel.note: Visually hides the label; it stays the accessible name. Use only when other visible text names the switch.

error.note: Error message. Setting it marks the field invalid.

size.note: Size step from the size vocabulary: medium (32x20 track) or small (24x16 track).

value.note: Submitted with the form while on.

checked.note: Current state (on). Not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset.

required.note: Native required: must be on. Adds an aria-hidden asterisk after the label.

disabled.note: Native disabled; dimmed; not submitted. A disabled fieldset ancestor has the same effect without changing the attribute.

anatomy.name: field
anatomy.notes: Grid: control in the first column, label, description and error in the second.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: Track wrapper; positions the thumb over the native input.

anatomy.name: input
anatomy.notes: Native <input type="checkbox" role="switch">; receives focus, Space and validation.

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: The sliding knob; decorative, follows the checked state.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: Native <label for> in the same shadow root.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Persistent polite live region; text appears when invalid.

input.note: Each toggle. Native and composed, so it crosses the shadow boundary.

change.note: Toggle committed. Re-dispatched from the host because native change is not composed (NativeControl).

focus-visible.note: 3px solid ring in ring color (a translucent ring would fall under 3:1).

checked.note: Track fills with primary; the thumb moves to the end (mirrored in rtl).

invalid.trigger: error set, or required and off after blur or a submit attempt

disabled.trigger: disabled attribute or a disabled fieldset ancestor

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop, through a native <label for> in the same shadow root.

formAssociation.note: FormAssociated + NativeControl: setFormValue(value) only while on, validity mirrored from the inner input (required -> valueMissing), formResetCallback restores the default checked attribute, a disabled switch (own or fieldset) is not submitted.

accessibility.targetSize: The track is 32x20 (24x16 small); the label is part of the clickable row, so the pointer target is the whole row (WCAG 2.5.8).
accessibility.focusRingVisible: On keyboard focus of the input; 3px ring in switch.focus-ring.color.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Dev-only console warning, once, when label is empty.

keyboard.Tab: move focus to and from the switch
keyboard.Enter: submits the form (implicit submission; the control has no form owner in its shadow root, SB-0009); it does not toggle

aria: native input with role=switch exposes its checked state as on/off
aria-describedby -> description and error ids (same root)
required: native required; the asterisk is aria-hidden
error: sets a customError validity, so the form blocks submission
the thumb is aria-hidden; state is never conveyed by color alone (the thumb position also changes)
announcements: error text is announced once when it appears (persistent aria-live=polite region)

useCases.when: An on/off setting that takes effect immediately or reads as a state (notifications, dark mode)
A setting needs its consequence explained
A setting must be on before submit
useCases.use: required with a label that states it

useCases.when: Space is tight, as in a dense settings row

antiPatterns.pattern: A switch for a choice recorded only on submit, or one of several options
antiPatterns.why: Switches read as an immediate setting; a choice made in a form reads as a checkbox

antiPatterns.pattern: Choosing exactly one option from several
A label that names the action ("Turn on") instead of the setting
antiPatterns.why: The label is the only name, and the on/off state is announced separately
antiPatterns.alternative: A label that names the setting

coverage: label is the name; label click toggles; role is switch
Space toggles; Enter does not toggle; keyboard focus ring
checked paints differently; the thumb moves
description and error in the accessible description; aria-invalid
required: native required, aria-hidden asterisk, invalid after blur
input and change composed, once per toggle
form: value only while on, custom value, reset to attribute default, validity, disabled fieldset and re-enable, error customError, label for, Enter submits, FormData read inside change

drift.contract: label, description and error are props of Switch
drift.realization: shadcn composes Field parts around Switch; shadow DOM requires them inside
shadcn default input track is neutral-200; changed for WCAG 1.4.11
not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset

openQuestions.question: Contract content drafted with the contract-author skill (visual reference, WAI-ARIA APG)?
openQuestions.answer: Yes: APG switch pattern, the visual reference for look and sizes, the Checkbox contract for the form and label shape.

openQuestions.question: Is checked reflected to an attribute?
openQuestions.answer: No, as in Checkbox: the attribute is the default that form reset restores (like native defaultChecked). Recommended for consistency with the sibling control.

openQuestions.question: Is label required?
openQuestions.answer: Yes, like Checkbox and Input; hide-label keeps it as the accessible name.

openQuestions.question: Native input type=checkbox with role=switch, or a div with role=switch?
openQuestions.answer: Native input with role=switch: keeps native Space, focus, required validity and the NativeControl mixin, with no ARIA state to maintain by hand.

openQuestions.question: Does Enter toggle?
openQuestions.answer: No. The APG makes Enter optional; Enter submits the form as in Checkbox (SB-0009), so a switch in a form behaves like the other controls.

openQuestions.question: Which sizes, under which names?
openQuestions.answer: medium (default) and small, from the shared size vocabulary (the older default and sm names map to them). Tracks of 32x20 and 24x16 come from the size.switch.* semantic tokens.

openQuestions.question: Is there an indeterminate state?
openQuestions.answer: No. A switch is on or off; a partial state belongs to Checkbox.

openQuestions.question: Does the switch take a label-position or a direction prop?
openQuestions.answer: No. The control sits before the label; thumb travel follows the inline direction with logical properties, so rtl needs no prop.
